line: Thirty-five hundred got him gone (Yeah) He got shanked by a lifer (21)
meaning: Lifer refers to someone in a prison system who is serving a life sentence without the option of parole. These people are more likely to shank (stab to kill) someone because you can’t increase your sentence if you’re never getting out, the payment of $3,500 is also so low because there is so little at stake, the consequences are being put in the hole/solitary confinement versus the potential of years being added to your sentence

line: Wish I could say who I’m smokin’, but honestly, never mind, it got too sticky (Shh)
vault_lines: Wish I could say who I'm smokin', but honestly, never mind, it got too sticky (Shh)
meaning:
While declining to mention who specifically, Savage claims he is smoking one of his opps, the act of figuratively disrespecting ones' deceased enemies while smoking marijuana. He previously referenced the concept of an “opp pack” on “Glock in My Lap,” a 2020 collaborative track with Metro Boomin:

I can’t smoke my opps (On God)
‘Cause all my opps is dust (Pussy)

21 further disrespects his opps by boasting about the stickiness of his weed. Sticky or gooey weed is desirable because it contained more resin in the flowers of the marijuana plant. Resin is a sap-like material that contains a lot of chemicals known as cannabinoids, these interact with receptors in your brain, making for a better high. In short, the stickier the weed, the higher you will become when consuming lesser quantities of it. Not only is the Atlanta native bragging about this strain of weed, but he puts down his enemies by co-signing its quality.

Encoded in these lines is the name of Drake’s 2022 studio album, Honestly, Nevermind and its seventh track, “Sticky.” 21 is a good friend of Drake’s, having been the sole feature on the aforementioned album, notably releasing a collab project with the Toronto rapper later that year, as well.
